review.raw_markdown:
--- # Skechers.com Mobile Journey Review **Persona: Walker Miles | 62-year-old Male | Skechers Plus Member** **Date: April 9, 2026 | Yesterday's Score: 4/10** --- ## 1. Executive Summary Mixed bag today, and one catastrophic failure that overshadows any progress. The Men's category navigation is clean and organized — I can find "Hands Free Slip-ins" quickly from the menu, and the product page is readable with the deal clearly shown. But the homepage still treats me like I don't exist (full Mother's Day pink takeover), the cart page is a blank white screen (complete failure), and a search for "slip in" shows me Women's products first — even though I'm logged in as a male customer. Yesterday was rough at 4/10. Today doesn't improve much, and the blank cart is actually a step backward. --- ## 2. Business Impact Score: 4/10 **No change from yesterday.** The cart failure alone is a conversion killer. I selected a shoe, tried to add it to cart, then hit a blank page. That's an abandoned purchase, full stop. No loyalty member should experience that. --- ## 3. What's Working - **BOGO 50% OFF deal is persistent** — that banner stays at the top of every screen. As a price-conscious guy, I appreciated seeing it constantly. Didn't have to hunt for the deal. - **Men's category navigation is solid** — clean list layout with "Hands Free Slip-ins" as a quick-tap shortcut right in the menu. No hunting required. Text is a good size, items are clearly separated. - **Product page is readable** — big bold product name, price front and center at $135, deal reminder ("Buy 1, Get 1 50% OFF! Applied at Cart"), and the Slip-ins badge. Felt like a real product page, not a cluttered mess. - **261 Slip-in results** — good inventory depth, and width filters (Wide Fit, Extra Wide Fit) are right at the top. That matters for a guy my age. - **ADD TO CART button** — large, navy blue, full-width. Easy to tap. No complaints there. --- ## 4. What's Weak - **Homepage: completely wrong audience** — I landed on a Mother's Day shop with a woman and little girl in pink flowers. I'm a 62-year-old man shopping for my own shoes. Not one piece of men's content above the fold. No "Welcome back, Walker." Nothing. I'm invisible. - **Login step didn't register visually** — the screenshot after "Log In" looks identical to the homepage. No confirmation, no name in the header, no "Hi Walker" or Skechers Plus indicator. I don't know if I'm even logged in. - **Cart page is a blank white screen** — this is the worst thing I saw today. I went through the whole process — found the shoe, looked at size options — and the cart rendered nothing. Zero. This is a broken purchase flow. A deal-breaker. - **Size grid is cramped** — 14 sizes in a grid on a phone screen. The boxes aren't terrible, but for my fingers they're borderline. I'd accidentally tap 10.0 when I meant 10.5. - **Search shows Women's first** — I searched "slip in" and got 1,024 results, but the first two visible products are both labeled "Women's." I'm logged in. Why am I seeing women's shoes? That's disrespectful to my time. - **No personalization anywhere** — not on homepage, not after login, not in search. A Skechers Plus member with purchase history should see something tailored. I got nothing. - **Popup dismiss step was invisible** — Step 2 looks identical to Step 1. Either there was no popup (fine) or it was dismissed so fast I couldn't see it. No issue either way, but the promo ticker text was cut off and unclear. --- ## 5. Recommendations 1. **Fix the cart immediately** — blank cart page is a P0 bug. Revenue is walking out the door on every session this happens. 2. **Personalize the homepage for logged-in members** — if I'm a Male Skechers Plus member who buys Slip-ins, show me men's content first. The Mother's Day banner can stay, but below a personalized hero. 3. **Show a logged-in confirmation** — add "Hi Walker" or a Plus member badge to the nav after login. I need to know my session is active. 4. **Fix search gender bias** — a logged-in male customer searching "slip in" should see Men's results first, not Women's. Simple personalization signal. 5. **Increase size selector tap targets** — slightly larger boxes or more spacing would reduce mis-taps for users my age. 6. **Surface Skechers Plus benefits earlier** — I'm a member. Remind me what I'm getting. Points balance, member pricing — none of that was visible. --- ## 6. Bottom Line The bones of a decent experience are there in the Men's navigation and product page. But the cart failing completely means I walked away without buying a $135 shoe I was ready to purchase. That's the whole ballgame. Until the cart works reliably and the homepage stops pretending I don't exist, this site is leaving loyal customers like me frustrated. **Score: 4/10. No improvement from yesterday.** --- ## 7. Evidence **Step 1 — Homepage** - Saw: BOGO 50% OFF bar at top, then a full-screen Mother's Day hero — woman, child, pink florals. "Get Mom a Gift She'll Love." SHOP NOW button. - Mobile use: Easy enough to see, but nothing to tap for men's content without scrolling far down. - Friction: Wrong audience. I'm a 62-year-old man. This homepage is talking to someone else. - Personalization: None. Felt completely generic. **Step 2 — Dismiss Popups** - Saw: Essentially same homepage. Promo ticker scrolled to show "Free Shipping with S..." (cut off). No modal or popup visible. - Mobile use: Fine, nothing to dismiss apparently. - Friction: Ticker text was truncated — I couldn't read the full free shipping offer without waiting for it to scroll. Annoying. - Personalization: None. **Step 3 — Log In** - Saw: Same homepage screenshot. No login form visible, no confirmation of login success, no change in header. - Mobile use: Can't evaluate — the login UI wasn't captured. - Friction: High uncertainty. I don't know if I'm actually logged in. No "Welcome back" message, no account name, no Plus member indicator in the nav icons. - Personalization: If I'm logged in, there's zero sign of it. **Step 4 — Men's Category** - Saw: Clean side-nav panel labeled "MEN" with: Shoes, Shop by Activity, Comfort Technologies, Collections, Collaborations, Clothing & Accessories. Quick-tap shortcuts at bottom: **Hands Free Slip-ins, Wide Fit, Extra Wide Fit.** - Mobile use: Very good. Simple list, generous row heights, easy to tap. This is how navigation should work for my age group. - Friction: None. This was the best screen of the whole journey. - Personalization: Not personalized but well-organized for my needs. **Step 5 — Men's Shoes (Hands Free Slip-ins)** - Saw: Category page with "Hands Free Slip-ins" heading, comfort tech description, width filter buttons (Wide Fit, Extra Wide Fit, Medium — third one slightly cut off by scrolling), 261 results, Filter + Sort by bar, first two shoes loading at bottom. - Mobile use: Good. Large heading text, clear breadcrumb (Men > Shoes). Width filters are a smart placement. - Friction: Medium — the third width filter button ("Medium") was cut off, suggesting a horizontal scroll I might not notice. - Personalization: No — no "Based on your history" or member sorting. **Step 6 — View Product** - Saw: MEN'S label, full product name ("Skechers Slip-ins: Max Cushioning Arch Fit 2.0 - Azusah"), 4-star rating, 10 reviews, Add to Wishlist, $135.00 price, BOGO deal reminder, Hands-Free Slip-ins badge, shoe image. - Mobile use: Excellent readability. Large text, clear price, deal is prominent. - Friction: Low. This was a clean, honest product page. - Personalization: No Plus member pricing or points-per-purchase callout. **Step 7 — Add to Cart** - Saw: Size grid (7.0–14.0 in 3 rows), "Please select a size" error in red/orange triangle, QTY dropdown, Ship it option, Check in-store availability, large ADD TO CART button. - Mobile use: Button is great — large, full-width, clear. Size grid is borderline — boxes are small for my fingers. - Friction: The "Please select a size" error is clear and visible. Good feedback. But I had to try before it told me — no pre-prompt to pick size before tapping Add to Cart. - Personalization: None — no "Your usual size is 11?" suggestion. **Step 8 — View Cart** - Saw: Completely blank white screen. Nothing. No products, no cart total, no error message, no loading spinner. - Mobile use: Impossible — the page didn't load. - Friction: Maximum. This is a catastrophic failure. I tried to buy a $135 shoe and the cart page broke. I'd close the app and not come back. - Personalization: Irrelevant — the page is broken. **Step 9 — Search** - Saw: "SLIP IN" as search heading (1,024 results). Filter + Sort by bar. First two visible products: **Skechers Slip-ins: Arch Fit Arcade - See Ya There (Women's)** and **Skechers Slip-ins: Contour Foam - Cozy Fit (Women's)**. Color swatches visible. Prices cut off at bottom. - Mobile use: Clean layout, two-column grid is readable. - Friction: High frustration. I searched for slip-ins as a logged-in male customer and the first results are Women's products. The site knows who I am (supposedly) and still leads with the wrong gender. - Personalization: Failed completely. Men's results should surface first. --- ## Technical Audit ## Technical Summary Platform: Salesforce Commerce Cloud (Demandware). Tag management via GTM (`GTM-TDRBQZ`). Consent via TrustArc (`vice-managed-src` pattern for deferred script injection). Bot protection via Kasada (`kpsdk-v=j-1.2.308`). Personalization via Monetate. Session replay via Quantum Metric. Style widget via Stylitics (broken). Eight-step funnel tested; LCP and CLS unmeasured across all steps. --- ## Accessibility 30 axe violations. Severity breakdown from available data: **Critical (4):** - `aria-required-children` — View Product: ARIA role used on parent without required child roles (e.g., `role="listbox"` missing `option` children) - `aria-valid-attr-value` — View Product: malformed ARIA attribute values (likely `aria-controls` or `aria-labelledby` pointing to non-existent IDs) - `button-name` — View Product: buttons rendered without accessible text (icon-only buttons with no `aria-label`) - `image-alt` — View Product: `` elements missing `alt` attribute, likely product images or swatches **Serious (5):** - `link-name` — Homepage: anchor tags with no inner text and no `aria-label` - `link-in-text-block` — Men's Shoes: links differentiated by color only, fails WCAG 1.4.1 - `aria-dialog-name` — View Product: modal/dialog missing `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` - `aria-input-field-name` — View Product: custom ARIA input widget unlabeled - `color-contrast` — View Product: foreground/background ratio below 4.5:1 (AA threshold) **Moderate (14+ across pages):** - Landmark structure broken sitewide: nested `
`, duplicate `
`, `
` not top-level, `
` not top-level (View Product), non-unique landmarks - `heading-order` violation on Homepage — heading levels skipped (e.g., `h1` → `h3`) - `aria-allowed-role` — Men's Shoes: `role` value invalid for the host element --- ## SEO - `` present, correct. - Multiple `async` third-party scripts will not block rendering but Googlebot may not fully execute all deferred content. - `tags.creativecdn.com/dhGobFICKSkk6J9nvQPw.js` loaded **twice** on Men's Category page — duplicate tag firing risk for conversion pixels. - `s.yimg.com/wi/ytc.js` loaded **twice** on all pages — duplicate Yahoo pixel events likely. - Demandware static JS (`us-skechers-prod.js`) loaded `async` on category pages only — inconsistent load pattern could affect event attribution. - Cart page returning HTTP 429 means cart content may be uncrawlable if Googlebot hits rate limits. --- ## Performance | Step | TTFB | LCP | CLS | |---|---|---|---| | Homepage | 125ms | — | — | | Log In | 41ms | — | — | | Men's Category | 41ms | — | — | | Men's Shoes | 36ms | — | — | | View Product | 29ms | — | — | | Add to Cart | 29ms | — | — | | View Cart | **141ms** | — | — | | Search | 32ms | — | — | - TTFB is acceptable across all steps. View Cart at 141ms is the outlier — consistent with the 429 errors hitting the cart endpoint and possible server-side session/cart hydration delay. - LCP and CLS not captured — critical gap. Product images (especially on View Product/Men's Shoes) are likely LCP candidates; image-alt violations suggest unoptimized img handling. - `--vh: 6.640000000000001px` set as inline style via JS on `` — this is a mobile viewport height workaround. Updating this on resize/scroll can trigger layout recalculations and contribute to CLS if done synchronously. - `webfontloader.js` (v1.6.28, from cdnjs) loaded async. Font-active classes (`wf-mulish-n4-active`, etc.) are on `` — FOUT possible if fonts race against first paint. This library is deprecated; native `font-display: swap` is the current standard. - Third-party script inventory is extremely heavy: GTM, TikTok pixel ×2 scripts, Pinterest, Snapchat, Reddit, Bing, Yahoo ×2, Impact, Tune (Go2SDK), Bloomreach, Quantum Metric, Monetate ×2 scripts, Taboola, NextDoor, Facebook, Stape, CreativeCDN ×2. Each is a separate network request and main-thread cost. --- ## Mobile Optimization - `--vh` custom property calculated in JS indicates awareness of the iOS Safari `100vh` bug. Correct approach, but floating-point precision artifact (`6.640000000000001px`) is benign unless used in pixel-snapped layouts. - No viewport `` visible in truncated source — could not verify `width=device-width, initial-scale=1` is set. Absence would be a critical mobile rendering failure; this must be confirmed. - `vice-managed-src` consent-deferred scripts load only after consent interaction — correct pattern for GDPR/CCPA compliance on mobile, but introduces timing variance in pixel fires. --- ## Console & Network Errors **HTTP 429 — Kasada fingerprint endpoint (5 hits):** ``` /149e9513-01fa-4fb0-aad4-566afd725d1b/2d206a39-8ed7-437e-a3be-862e0f06eea3/fp?x-kpsdk-v=j-1.2.308 ``` Kasada's client-side challenge script is rate-limiting its own fingerprint collection calls. This indicates either: (a) the challenge is being re-fired too aggressively by the Kasada JS, (b) the session token is expiring/invalid, or (c) the test environment IP was flagged. In production this can interrupt bot-protection telemetry and potentially degrade protected endpoint behavior. **HTTP 429 — Cart page:** ``` GET https://www.skechers.com/cart/ ``` The cart endpoint is rate-limited. This is a direct conversion blocker — users hitting this during normal browsing cannot load their cart. Whether this is infrastructure capacity, Kasada misclassifying legitimate users, or a CDN misconfiguration needs investigation. **CORS block — Stylitics (2 errors):** ``` Access to CSS stylesheet at 'https://web-assets.stylitics.com/style.css?...' blocked by CORS policy Access to XMLHttpRequest at 'https://web-assets.stylitics.com/style.css?...' blocked ``` The Stylitics outfit/look widget stylesheet is being fetched both as a `` and via XHR (likely a JS fallback), and both are blocked because `web-assets.stylitics.com` does not return `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://www.skechers.com`. The widget will render unstyled or not at all. Fix requires Stylitics to add the CORS header on their CDN — Skechers should file a ticket with their Stylitics account team. --- ## Recommendations 1. **[P0] Investigate cart 429s** — Determine if rate limiting is hitting real users or only automated test agents. If production-affecting, adjust Kasada thresholds or CDN rate limit rules for `/cart/`. 2. **[P0] Fix Stylitics CORS** — Coordinate with Stylitics to enable `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` for `skechers.com` on `web-assets.stylitics.com`. The XHR fallback pattern for a CSS file is also architecturally incorrect — stylesheets should not be fetched via XHR. 3. **[P1] Fix 4 critical axe violations on View Product** — `image-alt`, `button-name`, `aria-required-children`, `aria-valid-attr-value` are all WCAG 2.1 Level A failures. Product pages are highest-value; these also create legal exposure. 4. **[P1] Instrument LCP and CLS** — All 8 steps are missing these metrics. Integrate `web-vitals` JS library or expand RUM (Quantum Metric may already have this — confirm dashboards). Without CLS data, the `--vh` JS and font loading impact is unknown. 5. **[P1] Deduplicate third-party tags** — Remove duplicate `ytc.js` (Yahoo) and `tags.creativecdn.com` loads. Audit GTM container for double-firing triggers. Each duplicate fires inflated conversion event counts. 6. **[P2] Replace WebFontLoader** — Migrate to `@font-face` with `font-display: swap` in CSS. `webfontloader.js` is unmaintained and adds a network round-trip before fonts render. 7. **[P2] Resolve landmark structure violations** — Nested `
`, duplicate `
`, and misplaced `
`/`
` indicate template-level structural issues, likely in the Demandware page decorator layer. Fix in the base template affects all pages. 8. **[P3] Kasada 429s on fingerprint endpoint** — Review Kasada integration configuration. The challenge JS should not be triggering enough fingerprint requests to self-rate-limit within a single page session.
